algorithms.adaptation_note: Trains two arms of a 17,345-parameter position-slot MLP (no attention) from one initialization on four-digit sums mod 10: a direct-answer arm and a trace arm trained Nye-style on written partial sums along three fixed operand orders (L/R/T), so route diversity is built into the training data rather than sampled from a pretrained model; Wei et al.'s few-shot prompting is not implemented. The trace arm is decoded greedily and by self-consistency (40 samples at temperature 0.7, answer parsed after '#', majority vote with an Eq. 1 tie rule). History: a first single-route design was recorded as a design no-go (its vote tied greedy and a frozen trace-use criterion scored 0.351 against 0.80); the multi-route idea came only after seeing that result, so this design was pre-registered and evaluated once on a fresh multiset partition. Its defaults sit at the 150-epoch edge of the development grid (longer training not explored), and one frozen seed is shipped. On the pinned seed-42 CPython 3.12.8 Apple M1 Pro run the vote beats greedy by +0.104, partly by undoing greedy's poor route choice; over the best single forced route, chosen post hoc, the margin is +0.068. The vote costs 40 sampled traces and saturates near k = 20 (0.810, against 0.806 at k = 40). Trace versus direct on that run (+0.052, p = 0.083, unequal budgets; the direct arm differed slightly in one Ubuntu CI run) is not claimed. Faithfulness is only partial: the answer copies a written last sum in 0.831 of internally consistent corrupted traces, but later steps follow a corrupted first step only about 30-34% of the time. The held-out slice leans toward repeated digits. Toy scale: no emergence, faithful-reasoning, paper-scale or general-reasoning claim.
